label: early original-phase steps (t=1-4), boosted after z/b/m/e/w/k
explanation: A positional feature for the early original phase. Over 99% of activation mass falls on original-phase steps t=1-5, and t=3 alone carries 46%. It is never active at t=0, almost never active at the delimiter (0.8% of mass), and essentially silent in the copy phase or at t>=6. Within this window, rate and magnitude depend on which tokens were input before: z and b give about 4x lift as prev_tok and 3x as prev2_tok, m/e give about 3x, and w/k about 2x. The strongest activations (near max) come at t=3 right after a z/b pair (e.g. z b -> next token at about 1.0). The current input token matters little, and first occurrences are favored (91% of mass has in_first=1). Position alone (t=2-4) gives recall 0.91 but precision 0.35. Adding the requirement that one of z,b,m,e,w,k was seen earlier gives dev F1 about 0.67 and mass recall 0.88. The token dependence is graded rather than a clean set, so precision stays incomplete.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the previous input (most: z, b, m, e, w, k; least: n, c, i, 2) and the input two steps back (most: z, b, e, m, k, s; least: d, 2, y, i); timing cues that raise it most: t=3, t=4, t=2.
